routing_warnings.description: The rejected draft is specifically criticized for an indirect, weak hook and should not be treated as runtime evidence that the campaign-level CPL objective failed.
The CPL discussion supports changing the script's keywords rather than changing or runtime-testing the campaign-level performance objective.
The client evaluates the preview as below expectations and authorizes full production; this is not an executed campaign-performance result.
The 14-second duration applies to the preview draft, not the commissioned 30-second final-video package.
The client's rejection of generic terms and request for specific pain-point keywords primarily changes the product-keyword Requirement rather than audience demographics.
The preview failure concerns visual realism and obvious AI appearance rather than target-audience alignment.
The complaint that the content is not viral and does not match the required hooks primarily concerns the opening-hook Requirement.
The complaint that the preview looks unrealistic and obviously AI-generated concerns visual realism rather than reference alignment.
The reported failure concerns the draft's unrealistic, visibly AI-generated appearance rather than its testimonial narrative format.
The instruction changes the relationship to the reference video and does not explicitly remove or modify the testimonial format.
The client's observation that the preview looked unrealistic and immediately appeared AI-generated concerns visual realism rather than the preview workflow itself.
The client's observation that the preview had no attraction concerns creative performance rather than provision of the preview artifact.
This message requires both products to appear and belongs to the separate product-placement Requirement.
This progress report claims that the finalized script includes both products, but does not establish that the second product pack shot was generated or improved.
The message attributes poor retention to static imagery and insufficient scene cuts, supporting the editing and pacing Requirement rather than establishing a specific scene-generation method.
The complaint that the draft has no attraction concerns its attention-generating performance rather than visual realism specifically.
The request to recreate and improve the last reference changes the reference-alignment direction rather than the visual-realism requirement.
This message changes which product benefits should be incorporated rather than establishing a new keyword or wording constraint.
This progress claim primarily concerns beat-for-beat alignment with the reference video's sequence rather than specific keyword implementation.
The rejection of generic terms and request for specific Hindi keywords primarily changes script wording constraints rather than the underlying product benefits.
The prohibition on the word लिंग belongs to the script-wording Requirement; only the separate benefits-equivalence clause applies to the target Requirement.
